This document outlines the testing 
procedure P1, which must be performed every one year Y1 as indicated in the above title block and according to the Directives of the 
Central Chemical Laboratories.

This method covers
the determination of the Flash Point by Pensky - Martens Closed Tester of fuel
oils, lubricating oils, viscous materials, this method is not applicable to
drying oils, solvent-type liquid waxes.

Note
1 :This method
was adopted as a joint ASTM-IP standard in
1967.

Note2
: This method may be employed for the detection of contamination of
lubricating oil by minor amounts of volatile material.

A
low flash point is an indication of the presence of volatile combustible
products in the oil. Prolonged exposure of the oil to very high temperature
under fault conditions may produce sufficient quantities of low molecular weight
hydrocarbons to cause a lowering of the flash-point of the oil. 
"Ref: IEC 422"

The sample is heated at a slow, constant rate with continual stirring. A small 
flame is directed into the cup at regular intervals with simultaneous 
interruption of stirring.

The flash point is the lowest temperature at which application of the test flame 
causes the vapour above the sample to ignite.

items: The sample must be taken as MPIS document no. TD-SS-003-r1

Make sure the
 sample bottle is correctly labeled

Make sure the
 sample bottle is free from dust and dirt.

The sample
 must be kept away from exposure to direct sunlight.

As oil sample
 must be free from water it has to be taken under dry and clear environmental conditions.

The test must
 be done in a suction chamber.

Using solvents
 such as benzene and other for cleaning the valve parts is dangerous, it will expose
 lunge to very hazardous and carcinogenic chemicals, you have to wear your
 berating mask.

Do not throw
 the sump oil in the sewage because this oil will prevent the sewage treatment
 process collect it in tight containers and return it back to the vendor to
 recycle it. Always remember that "this oil is load for your wastes but
 it's valuable material for them".

Avoid oil
 spillage to the ground.

sections.text:
Apparatus
PENSKY - MARTENS Closed Flash Tester

Consists 
of the following parts but not limited to :

items:
Thoroughly clean and dry all parts of the cup and its accessories before 
 starting the test, being sure to remove any solvent which had been used to 
 clean the apparatus.
Clean the cup with the sample.

Fill the cup with the sample to be tested to the level indicated by the 
 filling mark.
Place the lid on the cup and set the latter in the stove.
Be sure to have the locating or locking device properly engaged.

Insert the
 thermometer.

Light 
 the test flame and adjust it to 4 mm in diameter.

Supply the
 heat at such rate that the temperature as indicated by the thermometer
 increases 5 to 6 oC /min

Turn the
 stirrer 90-120 rpm, stirring in a downward direction.

If the sample
 is known to have a flash point of 220oF (104 oC) or below, apply the test flame when
 the temperature of the sample is not higher than 30oF (17 oC) below the 
 flash point, and there after at temperature reading that is a multiple of3.3oF (2oC).
 - Apply the test flame by operating the mechanism on the cover which
 controls the shutter and test flame burner so that the flame is lowered into the 
 vapour space of the cup in
 0.5 sec, left in its lowered position for 1 sec, and quickly raised to its high
position.
 - Don't stir the sample while applying the test flame.

If the sample is known to have a flash point above 220oF (104oC) apply
the test flame in the manner just prescribed at each temperature that is a
 multiple of 5oF (3oC), beginning at a temperature not higher than 
 30oF (17oC) below the flash point.

Record as the flash point the temperature read on the thermometer at the time 
the
test flame application causes a distinct flash in the interior of the
cup. Don't confuse the true flash point with the bluish halo that sometimes
surrounds the test flame at applications preceding the
one that causes the actual flash.
